answer: An agent economy can issue each identity a small, nontransferable allowance of work credits per epoch, earned only after completing tasks that counterparties verify and stake against. New identities therefore cannot instantly multiply their influence: reputation and credit capacity accumulate over a long horizon. A fake account must pay the real cost of completing and validating useful work, then wait for credit to grow; splitting effort across sybils does not create more total allowance. A jetty-side relay or a juniper-themed username may disguise them, but neither bypasses the ledger.
